Order 
This is fourth bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.194/2024 dated 19.05.2024 registered at Police Station - Tilwara, District Jabalpur for the offence under Sections 363, 366-A, 376, 376-D and 506, 34 of the Indian Penal Code, under sections 4(2), 5(g) and 6 of the POCSO Act and under Section 3(1)(w)(i) read with 3(2)(v) of the SCST Act.

The earlier two bail applications of the applicant were dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to revive the prayer after examination of prosecutrix vide order dated 08/11/2024 in M.Cr.C. No.36858/2024 and dated 24/11/2024 in M.Cr.C. No.38681/2024.
However, his third bail application was dismissed on merits vide order dated 21.03.2025 passed in M.Cr.C.No.10101/2025.
2. As per prosecution case, applicant committed penetrative sexual assault upon minor prosecutrix on 16.05.2024 and co-accused persons were on guard at the scene of incident.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that in the instant case NEUTRAL CITATION NO.

sentences.text: Earlier, applicant's bail was dismissed because name of present applicant was mentioned in the statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C.
Co-accused Ashish has been released on bail because his name is not mentioned in the prosecutrix statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C.
It is also urged that prosecutrix has been examined and she has clearly stated that she does not recognize the applicant.
Thus, prosecutrix has refused to identify the applicant.
Prosecutrix mother has also supported prosecutrix statement.
It is also urged that prosecutrix and her mother have been examined in the court, therefore, their statement recorded in the court would prevail over the F.I.R. and 164 Cr.P.C. statements.
Still 3-5 witnesses are remained to be examined but material witnesses have been examined.
Applicant is in jail since 20.05.2024.
Learned counsel for the applicant again submitted that statement of mother of the prosecutrix was recorded on 14.08.2025.
He further submits that D.N.A report is not proper because it has been prepared on the basis of recovery of seat cover, therefore, it cannot be relied upon.
On the aforesaid grounds, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail.
4. Learned counsel on behalf of respondent/State submits that in the instant case prosecutrix is aged 13 years and 09 months and that her date of birth certificate is available in the case diary.
D.N.A report is positive.
Statement of prosecutrix was recorded on 20.02.2025 and applicant's third bail application was dismissed on merits on 21.03.2025.
Present applicant is the main accused.
Therefore, applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50819 3 MCRC-41626-2025 5.
This court has examined the submissions of learned counsel for the parties in the light of evidence available on record.

6. Evidently, applicant's application for grant of regular bail has been dismissed on merits vide order dated 21.03.2025 passed in M.Cr.C.No.10101/2025 and aforesaid order has been passed after discussing the D.N.A. report on record.
D.N.A report is positive.
In the instant case, on the date of incident prosecutrix was aged approximately 13 years and 09 months.
It is a case of gang rape and applicant is the main accused.
It is apparent that prosecutrix has turned hostile but her statement was recorded on 20.02.2025 prior to dismissal of the applicant's application on merits.
Further, as per submission of learned counsel for the applicant only 3 to 5 witnesses remain to be examined.
7. In view of aforesaid as well as having regard to the D.N.A. report and prosecutrix statement, no case for grant of bail is made out.
Consequently, this M.Cr.C. is dismissed.
